data.title: The forecast is systematically biased
data.body: At the 09:00 D-1 cutoff the forecast ran on average 1,748 MW above actual wind, so buying against it leaves the desk short more often than long.

data.title: Errors are largest on windy days
data.body: On windy days the bias was 2,505 MW (MAE 2,576 MW); on calm days 1,065 MW (MAE 1,707 MW). Curtailment of wind farms on the windiest days is one likely cause.

data.title: The forecast beats a naive guess
data.body: Its error is 49 % smaller than assuming tomorrow repeats today (persistence MAE 3,980 MW).

data.title: Deciding later barely helps
data.body: Waiting from 09:00 to 11:00 switches to the 09:30 vintage and changes MAE by -26 MW (-1.3 %).

data.title: A P90 margin of 4.1 GW
data.body: Buying against forecast minus 4,140 MW of wind would have covered 90 % of half-hours in hindsight, but 85.2 % when each day's margin is set only from days already known at its cutoff.

data.title: A smarter margin cuts over-buying by 16 %
data.body: Varying the margin with the forecast level gave 85.1 % coverage (flat: 85.2 %) with 1,114 GWh over-procured (flat: 1,331 GWh), out of sample.
